title: Organization key document
description:
The signed statement binding an organization to its signing keys and the namespaces it owns (publisher-trust spec §2). Fetched by a client, signed by the repository ROOT key.

THE PAYLOAD IS CARRIED AS OPAQUE BYTES ON PURPOSE. The signature covers the decoded `payload` exactly as transmitted, so there is no canonical-JSON step: signer and verifier never have to agree on key order, whitespace, or number formatting. Signing a parsed-and-re-serialized object is a well-known source of signature-bypass bugs, and this format makes that class of mistake unrepresentable.

format.description: Envelope version. A client that does not recognise the value refuses the document rather than guessing at its meaning.

root-key-id.description: Which root key signed this, so a client holding several roots knows which to check and can report the answer (spec §6.3).

payload.description: base64 of the UTF-8 JSON described by $defs/document.

signature.description: base64 ed25519 signature over the DECODED payload bytes.

organization.description: The organization this document speaks for.

namespaces.description: Dotted name prefixes this organization owns. Matched SEGMENT-AWARE (spec §4.3.1): `dev.cajeta` owns `dev.cajeta.http` and does NOT own `dev.cajetaevil`. At least one is required — a document owning nothing can authorise nothing.

not-after.description: Document expiry (spec §2.5). A client refuses an expired document however it was obtained, including from cache.

keys.description: The organization's signing keys. More than one with overlapping windows is what makes rotation possible without a flag day (spec §2.6).

id.description: Stable identifier, so revocation and audit can name a key.

public-key.description: PEM SubjectPublicKeyInfo, the form `cajeta archive sign` and the trust store already use.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 in UTC, seconds precision, `Z` only. Offsets are rejected rather than converted: a validity window is a security boundary, and accepting several spellings of one instant invites the parser and the signer to disagree.
